C0.quote: it is an instance of committee elections, where the statements play
C0.note: Proportional slate selection, cast as a committee election or participatory-budgeting-style aggregation of agents' utilities.

C1.quote: establish its proportionality guarantees under approximate queries
C1.note: Main theoretical results are approximate cBJR guarantees and impossibility results for a query-based algorithm. There are also synthetic simulations (Sec 3.4) and LLM experiments on real drug-review and Polis data (Sec 4).

C2.1.value: utility function u_i (accessed via discriminative/generative queries); in implementation, "textual information" about each user
C2.1.quote: each agent i ∈ N has a utility function ui : U → [r]

C2.2.quote: mapping each statement α ∈ U to one of r possible utility values
C2.2.note: OTH: in the implementation, the input is unstructured text (reviews, comments) from which LLM queries estimate utilities.

C2.3.quote: we are provided with textual information reflecting their opinions
C2.3.note: Agents have utility functions and opinions.

C2.4.quote: we are provided with textual information reflecting their opinions
C2.4.note: The procedure works on user texts and query outputs, which are separate from the true utilities u_i. Disc(i, α) is notated separately and may differ from u_i(α). The difference is due to estimation error, not misreporting. IDU also partly fits; the doubt rule selects the first listed code.

C3.2.note: The paper never states that users' submitted texts truthfully report their opinions. It only says the text reflects their opinions.

C4.1.note: Input format is cardinal or text, not ordinal or approval.

C4.2.note: The term 'dichotomous preferences' is not used.

C5.1.quote: To evaluate whether a slate adequately represents the agents
C5.1.note: Evaluation uses cBJR proportionality and agents' utilities (mean and 25th percentile).

C5.2.quote: treat them as the true, underlying utilities
C5.2.note: Theory evaluates on true u_i, separate from query outputs. Experiments evaluate on CoT utilities treated as proxies for true utilities.

VOT.note: In the formal model (Sections 2-3) agents only have utility functions that are accessed through queries; they take no action. Review and comment submission happens in the datasets, outside the model.

claims.quote: demonstrating its effectiveness in generating representative slates from unstructured user opinions
PROSE outperforms four baseline approaches with respect to both user satisfaction
a compelling vision for how AI can support democratic innovation

C9.2.quote: Consequently, we rely on a proxy.
C9.2.note: Needed assumptions: user texts reflect opinions (stated, Sec 2) and CoT utilities stand in for true utilities (stated as a proxy, Sec 4.2.3). No separate sincerity or strategic-behaviour assumption is needed beyond the stated link between texts and opinions.

C2.4.reason: The paper keeps the texts and query outputs the procedure uses separate in notation and wording from the agents' true utilities and opinions, which meets the DIST condition.

C6.VOT.reason: The formal model has agents whose utilities are queried, not agents who take an action, so voters are not present under the C6 definition.

C9.2.reason: The assumptions needed for the satisfaction and representation claims, namely that texts reflect opinions and that the CoT proxy stands for true utilities, are both stated in the paper.
